note: State officials attributed the DMV breach to credentials stored on a police employee’s personal device, making this a concrete example of credential hygiene and access-scoping failure.

note: Wiz observed attackers chaining an authentication bypass with token-scope validation flaws to obtain administrator control and deploy persistent backdoors.

title: Stolen AI Session Tokens Are Bypassing MFA
note: Research note connects infostealer-compromised AI-service and enterprise SSO tokens to MFA bypass and highlights session lifecycle and token-revocation requirements for AI identities.

title: Trezor Says 347,000 Users Received Phishing Emails After Brevo Hack
note: Brevo’s incident illustrates how an attacker-created SSO configuration and invited-user trust can turn federation behavior into account access and downstream phishing capability.

title: Surfshark Systems Targeted by Hackers
note: An internet-exposed engineering test server contained committed build credentials, illustrating how misconfiguration and exposed secrets can create identity-control risk even when production user data is segregated.

title: Attacker gained access to client accounts
note: Brevo’s postmortem identifies a federation-boundary failure in which an attacker’s SSO configuration granted access to invited users across organizations rather than only the owning tenant.

title: Cisco FMC flaws exploited by ransomware gang, state-sponsored hackers
note: Exploitation of an authentication bypass and static-credential flaw in Cisco FMC enabled credential theft, discovery of Active Directory service-account secrets, lateral access and ransomware deployment.

title: The Machine With Many Faces: Post-Exploitation Identity Misuse in SPIFFE/SPIRE
note: Unit 42 details how root access on a Kubernetes node can enable spoofing or harvesting of co-located workload identities through SPIFFE/SPIRE metadata.

title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026
note: Anthropic’s threat report details AI-assisted intrusions built around stolen credentials, API keys, session tokens, cloud secrets and OAuth fan-out, including operational indicators useful to defenders.

title: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
note: Microsoft documents AI-themed campaigns that steal credentials and access tokens, including a business-email-compromise case using OAuth device-code phishing without conventional password theft.

title: The Top 4 Threats We Found by Investigating Every Alert for a Quarter
note: A field-based threat report finds authenticated-session hijacking, token replay, MFA bypass, OAuth consent, and persistence surviving password resets among the dominant identity attack patterns.

title: OAuth Authorization Request Delegation Chain
note: This new OAuth draft proposes signed, hash-linked delegation chains so upstream authorization servers can evaluate downstream clients and intermediary brokers before issuing tokens.

title: How Privileged Can Your AI Become? More Than You Might Think
note: A useful practitioner framing of privilege as dynamic and contextual for agents that can call tools, discover paths and expand effective reach during execution.

title: Implementer’s Draft of OpenID Connect Key Binding Approved
note: The OpenID Foundation approved the first Implementer’s Draft of OpenID Connect Key Binding, relevant to binding tokens more strongly to cryptographic keys and reducing replay risk.

title: One Click to Leak: Characterizing the Real-World Usage and Threat Impact of MNO-based Single Sign-On Websites
note: This measurement study finds widespread trust defects in web-based mobile-network SSO, including exposed developer credentials and high-privilege tokens issued before user consent, with observed exploitation at scale.

title: Signing the Transaction but Not the Decision: Whisper Attacks and a Binding Defense for AP2
note: The paper shows that cryptographically valid agent-payment signatures may fail to bind the user’s actual decision, enabling prompt or content-driven credential access and unauthorized purchases, and proposes capability-binding defenses.

title: Security Advisory Summary: September 2026
note: Okta discloses newly identified vulnerabilities affecting Access Gateway, Hyperdrive Agent, Privileged Access, and Okta Verify for Windows, with updates required and no observed exploitation.

title: Introducing the Google Cloud Developer Plugin for AI Coding Agents
note: Google’s new agent plugin packages authentication, authorization, project-management skills, and guardrails intended to reduce accidental key exposure and unsafe gcloud operations by coding agents.

title: Singapore expands Singpass passkeys to Android users
note: Useful deployment signal for practitioners: Singapore expanded national-ID passkeys to Android after reporting roughly 800,000 registered passkeys during the initial rollout.

title: Switching password managers is easy and safe on Android
note: Google announced Android support for direct password and passkey transfers between credential managers, materially advancing deployment and lifecycle considerations around FIDO Credential Exchange.

title: Secure AI Coding: Governing every agent, artifact, and identity
note: The product move is relevant because coding agents increasingly operate with human identity, filesystem, terminal and business-system access, requiring task-scoped identities and removal of standing privilege.

title: Closing the frontline MFA coverage gap with Okta NFC
note: Introduces badge-and-PIN authentication for shared frontline workstations, with individually attributable access and automated provisioning and deprovisioning.

title: Passkey-themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise
note: Microsoft documents active campaigns combining passkey-themed impersonation, device-code phishing, AiTM session theft, attacker-added MFA methods, Graph reconnaissance and cloud data collection.

title: Signing in without actually signing in
note: Okta analyzes infostealer data containing reusable session tokens and API keys, a strong reminder that authenticated state can be stolen and replayed without a fresh sign-in.

title: Active exploitation of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center vulnerabilities
note: Talos identifies in-the-wild exploitation of an authentication bypass and static-credential flaw that enabled root access, credential harvesting, tunneling, and ransomware or destructive malware deployment.

title: Security update: September 2026 incident report
note: Affected-party disclosure tracing unauthorized access to an exposed internal test server and build-related credentials that required rotation and token revocation.

title: AdaptHealth confirms 4.1 million people exposed in July cyberattack
note: AdaptHealth said a social-engineering attack compromised a privileged third-party contractor account and exposed data from cloud business applications and clinical portals.

title: MFA's Weakest Link: Account Recovery Is the New Attack Path
note: The analysis ties recent Scattered Spider-style intrusions to social-engineered password and MFA resets, treating service-desk recovery as part of the authentication boundary.

title: New Okta innovations close governance blind spots and extend zero standing privilege to secure the agentic enterprise
note: A significant platform move combining AWS entitlement management, access-drift remediation, privileged access, and identity-threat capabilities for human, machine, and AI-agent identities.

title: Inside the underground market for AI access
note: Okta documents the criminal market for hijacked AI accounts and trial credits, including account takeover, stolen credentials, and machine-access resale dynamics.
